A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LoOT-Free expert-advice research. The main text, algorithms, mathematical results, Table 1, Figures 1–4, and Appendices A–F support a reliable comparison despite repagination and relocation.

before.justification: Appendix F reports original synthetic-loss experiments comparing LoOT-Free OMD/FTRL with Squint, AdaHedge, and exponential weights, with results over 40 repetitions in Figures 1–4.

after.justification: Appendix F retains these original synthetic-loss experiments and their reported outcomes in Figures 1–4.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3 retain their clipping, rescaling, learning-rate definitions, and prediction updates. The FTRL pseudocode moves from Appendix C into Section 5.2 without changing the procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix F retains the same synthetic heavy-tailed and non-heavy-tailed loss scenarios. Newly cited financial, electricity-forecasting, and web-view applications expand motivation only.

E2.justification: Both experimental regimes retain the same evaluated comparators: Squint with the improper prior, AdaHedge, and the specified exponential-weights implementation.

E3.justification: Both versions use K in {15, 25, ..., 135}, T = 20K, the same loss-generation distributions, and the same loss metric. EW and Squint receive the maximum loss in both versions.

E4.justification: The comparisons between the two loss regimes and associated discussion of algorithm failures and Squint's behavior are retained. No ablations, sensitivity tests, or additional robustness analyses are introduced.

E5.justification: Figures 1–4 retain reporting over 40 repetitions, and Figures 2 and 4 retain mean plus or minus one standard deviation. Replacing the caption wording with the ± symbol does not change uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Figures 1–4 contain identical plotted results, including their uncertainty curves and rankings. The corresponding experimental findings are unchanged, with no added or removed result entries.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 adds a derivation showing that i.i.d. losses satisfy the self-bounding condition with C = 0. Appendix C clarifies prerequisites used in the FTRL bound; the theorem bounds remain unchanged. New R_T equalities in Equations (2) and (4) conflate realized regret with the introductory expectation-based definition.

C1.justification: The introduction corrects reversed algorithm attributions: Algorithm 2 receives the optimal worst-case guarantee, and Algorithm 1 receives the self-bounded guarantee. This aligns the contribution summary with the unchanged Theorems 2.2 and 2.4; the abstract's central claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations of heavy-tail failures and Squint's behavior, along with the stated limitations and future directions, are retained. The new i.i.d. derivation supports the stochastic applicability already claimed in the abstract and Appendix B.2.

D1.justification: Loss-generation rules, baseline parameter information, line-search implementation guidance, and the MacBook Air M2 with 8GB RAM disclosure are retained. Moving the hardware disclosure does not add reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The introduction adds application references by Bradley and Taqqu, Cha et al., Devaine et al., and Li and Jones. Section 3 also adds Cesa-Bianchi et al. (1997). Existing novelty positioning and substantive comparisons remain stable; other reference updates concern the same works.

P1.justification: The revision makes limited prose, notation, and cross-reference edits, updates author information, and adds acknowledgements. Existing Fréchet material receives a separate Appendix A.2 heading, while the overall narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: Table 1 changes its ruling and column presentation, Algorithm 2 moves into the main text, and the experimental figures are resized and repositioned with minor caption edits. The existing displays retain their substantive content.

improvement.justification: Corrected algorithm attributions, the explicit i.i.d. self-bounding derivation, and placement of FTRL pseudocode beside its analysis modestly improve clarity and accessibility. These gains outweigh the limited expected-versus-realized regret inconsistency introduced in Equations (2) and (4). The principal theoretical guarantees and empirical evidence are unchanged.
